* Base class for every error the chatbot raises on purpose.

*

It is a checked exception (it extends Exception, not RuntimeException) because
* callers are expected to react to it: the compiler forces them to either handle it or declare
* it. Code should generally throw one of the two subclasses rather than this class directly,
* since the subclass is what tells the caller how to react.
* Creates an exception that remembers the lower-level exception that triggered it.

*

Always prefer this constructor when converting one exception into another. Without the
* cause, the original stack trace is lost and "Error saving to storage" is all you ever get
* @param msg   message shown to the user
* @param cause the original exception being translated
* Signals that the user typed something the chatbot cannot make sense of, such as an unknown
* command, a missing argument, or a task number that does not exist.

*

This is an expected, recoverable situation: the caller should show the message and carry
* on reading commands. Nothing is broken.
* Signals that reading or writing the save file failed, or that its contents are corrupted.

*

Unlike {@link FoodInputException} this is not the user's fault and retrying the same
* command will not help. The caller should report it and stop, rather than carry on accepting
* commands whose changes can no longer be saved.
